open_points.subject: owner-session monotonic instants
open_points.text: its instants — when it began, its last request, when its confirmation was shown — and its expiry at the latest are held as readings of that monotonic clock
open_points.question: What representation and comparison arithmetic must be used for monotonic readings held in an owner session?
options: integer monotonic ticks with a declared unit and range
a monotonic-duration value supplied by the clock backend
an implementation-native numeric reading whose unit and precision are unspecified
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque monotonic-duration value from `clock`, with duration addition and strict comparisons performed without conversion to UTC.

witness.initial: A valid owner session is one microsecond short of its 30-minute idle limit.
events: The process clock supplies a reading whose native resolution or numeric unit is not specified.
Registry converts or compares that reading to the 30-minute constant.
outcomes: A representation preserving microseconds admits the request.
A coarser or differently converted representation refuses the request at the boundary.

open_points.subject: time readings per owner-session operation
open_points.text: Both readings reach the code through `clock` alone, emitted from the `system_clock_backend` IR whose `time_source_policy` the data closure declares (SPEC_STANDARD §6.8).
open_points.question: For sign-in, request admission, confirmation creation or submission, sign-out, and the 60-second session pass, how many monotonic and wall-clock readings does one operation take, and which facts and comparisons share each reading?
options: one monotonic reading per operation, shared by all of that operation's session comparisons and writes, plus one wall-clock reading only when it records a durable instant
separate readings for each comparison and each written fact
a separately stated reading rule for each operation
open_points.default_guess: Take one monotonic reading at the operation's decision point and reuse it for every session comparison and runtime instant that operation changes; take one UTC reading for all durable instants written by one transaction.

witness.initial: A request begins immediately before the idle limit, and its confirmation step is created immediately after the limit would be reached by a second clock read.
events: The owner submits a request that both refreshes the session and creates a pending confirmation.
Registry checks validity and records the request and confirmation times.
outcomes: With one shared reading, the request is admitted and both runtime instants use the pre-limit reading.
With multiple readings, the session check may pass while the confirmation time or another comparison uses a post-limit reading.
witness.observer: the owner and a later confirmation submission

open_points.subject: lockout boundary required test
open_points.text: The sixth sign-in within 15 minutes after five refusals is refused with the right credential, and accepted 15 minutes later.
open_points.question: Is “15 minutes later” measured from the fifth refusal that started the lockout, from the refused sixth attempt, or from another stated instant?
options: exactly 15 minutes after the fifth refusal
exactly 15 minutes after the sixth attempt
15 minutes after whichever attempt the test harness most recently made
open_points.default_guess: Measure from the fifth refusal, because rule 3 says that refusal starts the lockout and later attempts do not extend it.

witness.initial: Five wrong credentials are refused at 12:00 and the right credential is attempted at 12:14.
events: The fifth refusal starts the lockout at 12:00.
The sixth attempt is refused at 12:14.
The owner retries at 12:15 and at 12:29.
outcomes: If measured from the fifth refusal, the 12:15 attempt is accepted.
If measured from the sixth attempt, acceptance waits until 12:29.

open_points.subject: clock delivery contract
open_points.text: Both readings reach the code through `clock` alone, emitted from the `system_clock_backend` IR whose `time_source_policy` the data closure declares (SPEC_STANDARD §6.8).
open_points.question: What exact module contract delivers `clock` to each operation that reads time?
options: a datetime or monotonic reading parameter on each mutating operation
a clock port supplied through the owning object's constructor
a declared authority module imported by consumers
open_points.default_guess: Use a clock port supplied through construction so tests can replace both readings together.
consequences: A per-call parameter makes every reading explicit but enlarges operation signatures.
Constructor injection centralizes the authority and supports replacement in tests.
An authority module minimizes signatures but creates a shared dependency that State 7 notes must name correctly.
open_points.requirement: Both readings reach the code through `clock` alone, emitted from the `system_clock_backend` IR whose `time_source_policy` the data closure declares (SPEC_STANDARD §6.8).

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: The mapping names the file by its digest.
open_points.question: What bytes or logical content are digested, which digest algorithm is required, and what representation is stored and compared?
options: digest the exact uploaded file-part bytes with a named cryptographic algorithm and canonical encoding
parse the file and digest a canonical serialization of its logical records
leave the algorithm, input normalization and representation to generation
open_points.default_guess: Digest the exact file-part bytes with SHA-256 and store and compare a fixed lowercase hexadecimal encoding.

witness.initial: A session holds file A and a confirmation bound to its digest; file B has different bytes but equivalent parsed records, or collides under a weak or implementation-chosen digest.
events: The owner is shown the mapping for file A.
The confirmation is submitted while Registry resolves the kept file by the unspecified digest rule.
outcomes: A raw-byte cryptographic digest binds the confirmation only to file A's exact bytes.
A canonical-content or weak digest can treat file B as having the same identity and apply bytes the owner was not shown.

open_points.subject: accepted import timestamps
open_points.text: A Customer the import makes is created at the import's instant with revision 1.
open_points.question: Does one accepted import take one UTC wall-clock reading shared by every new Customer, the migration closure and its audit entry, or may those records carry different readings taken during the transaction?
options: one UTC reading shared by all facts written by the import transaction
one reading per record
separate readings for customer creation, closure success and audit change
open_points.default_guess: Take one UTC reading after admission and reuse it throughout the transaction.

witness.initial: An accepted import spans a UTC clock tick or a backward wall-clock adjustment.
events: Registry writes the migration closure and the one audit entry in the same transaction.
outcomes: One reading gives every imported Customer, the closure and the audit entry one import instant.
Several readings give them different or non-monotonic instants despite one accepted transaction.
witness.observer: the owner reading the imported Customers and audit log

open_points.subject: migration export format
open_points.text: A file that cannot be read as the format States 5 and 6 declare, that holds two project records with one id, or a project record whose id or status is missing or cannot be read, is refused whole at upload, before anything is picked.
open_points.question: What exact file structure, field representation and decoding rules define a readable migration export?
options: one versioned JSON document with arrays of each record kind
newline-delimited versioned records
a versioned archive containing separate files per record kind
open_points.default_guess: Use one versioned JSON document with explicit schemas and unambiguous UTC and identifier encodings.
consequences: A single document simplifies whole-file validation but may require holding the parsed structure in memory.
Line-delimited records support streaming but require explicit ordering and cross-record validation rules.
An archive separates record kinds but adds entry-name, duplication and archive-safety decisions.
open_points.requirement: Registry checks what the picks bring in — each picked project with the rooms and pointers that name it and the v1 value it names — and nothing else of the file;

open_points.subject: non-text stored values rendered in the owner interface
open_points.text: a value that is not text in the text it is shown as
open_points.question: What exact textual representation must the owner interface show for each non-text stored type, including identifiers, booleans or marks, ordinals, dates, UTC instants, absent values and byte digests?
options: a canonical representation declared per domain type
the language or template engine's default string conversion
localized display text chosen by each page
open_points.default_guess: Declare one canonical representation per domain type, using model vocabulary names, decimal ordinals, ISO 8601 UTC instants, ISO dates and a fixed digest encoding.

witness.initial: An audit entry contains a UTC instant and an ordinal sequence number, and a Customer contains an absent fiscal value.
events: The owner opens two pages that show those stored non-text values.
Each page converts the values to text.
outcomes: Canonical per-type rendering shows the same stable text on both pages.
Default or localized conversion can show different time zones, boolean words, absent-value markers or number formatting.

set_aside.subject: store command lowering
set_aside.text: How the store's backend lowers this is the backend's.
set_aside.question: Which backend mechanism ensures caller values fill only value places and never alter command structure?
options: native prepared statements with bound parameters
a typed query builder that emits bound parameters
a backend API whose command and value channels are structurally separate
set_aside.default_guess: Use native bound parameters through the single statement backend and prohibit interpolation in generated store commands.
consequences: Prepared statements give a direct structural separation but must cover every command path.
A typed builder can enforce the rule compositionally but its escaping and identifier APIs must be constrained.
A custom separated API can centralize enforcement but adds code whose correctness factory checks must establish.
set_aside.requirement: A value a caller gives only ever fills a value place of a query or command whose structure the release fixes; it never becomes an identifier, an operator or syntax.
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: script prohibition in owner pages
set_aside.text: The owner interface sends no script of its own (R0-29) and forbids the browser to run any, by its content security policy.
set_aside.question: What exact response policy and page-generation constraints enforce the no-script guarantee?
options: a `Content-Security-Policy` response header with `script-src 'none'` on every owner page
the equivalent CSP delivered in HTML plus a generator prohibition on script-bearing markup
a shared response wrapper that applies an equivalent stricter policy to all owner-interface responses
set_aside.default_guess: Apply a response-header CSP containing `script-src 'none'` through the shared owner-page response path and generate no script-bearing elements or event-handler attributes.
consequences: A response header is applied before HTML parsing and can be checked uniformly.
An HTML-delivered policy depends on correct placement and still requires markup restrictions.
A shared wrapper reduces omissions but factory checks must establish that every owner page uses it.
set_aside.requirement: The owner interface sends no script of its own (R0-29) and forbids the browser to run any, by its content security policy.
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change
